ContractDiffOut.description:
The classified changes between two refs, computed on the fly and never stored.

``changes`` items have the stored-report change shape: ``code``, ``class``,
``element_kind``, ``path``, ``pointer_before``, ``pointer_after``, ``attribute``, ``before``,
``after`` (values only for allow-listed attributes).
ContractDiffOut.title: ContractDiffOut

ContractDiffSideOut.description: One side of a diff: the ref as named and the version or draft it resolved to.
ContractDiffSideOut.title: ContractDiffSideOut

ContractLatestVersionOut.description: The contract's Latest published version (lifecycle metadata, not document content).
ContractLatestVersionOut.title: ContractLatestVersionOut

ContractListOut.description: A page of contracts. There is deliberately no total or count (it would leak existence).
ContractListOut.title: ContractListOut

ContractTemplateOriginOut.description: The template version a contract was copied from; the content is not linked.
ContractTemplateOriginOut.title: ContractTemplateOriginOut

ContractValidationReportOut.description:
The stored validation report a version was published with.

``report`` is validation's report, passed through as JSON with its ``compatibility`` and
``ref_facts`` sections; ``pins`` are the rule-set versions it was validated against.
ContractValidationReportOut.title: ContractValidationReportOut

ContractVersionListOut.description: Every visible version, highest SemVer precedence first (unpaginated).
ContractVersionListOut.title: ContractVersionListOut

ContractVersionMetadataOut.description: One visible version of a contract, without its document.
ContractVersionMetadataOut.title: ContractVersionMetadataOut

ContractVersionOriginOut.description:
The contract version or draft a contract was copied from; the content is not linked.

``version_id`` is provenance only: it names a version or draft of the source contract at the
time of the copy.
ContractVersionOriginOut.title: ContractVersionOriginOut

ContractVersionSummaryOut.description:
A contract's head version.

``deprecated`` is lifecycle metadata like ``state``: true when the head version is deprecated,
and returned to metadata-only callers too.
ContractVersionSummaryOut.title: ContractVersionSummaryOut

IdentityAuthPolicyOut.description: What a sign-in screen may know before anyone is signed in.
IdentityAuthPolicyOut.title: IdentityAuthPolicyOut

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details. Extensions such as report, run_id and reasons may appear.
Problem.title: Problem

get.description:
List and search contracts: filters, ``q`` text match, keyset pagination.

``sort`` is ``id`` (the default, creation order) or ``name`` (lower-cased name, an empty name
sorted by its odcs id, then id); ``next_cursor`` is only valid with the ``sort`` it came from.

``require("contract:list")`` admits every authenticated caller; the identity scopes below trim
the SQL, so a caller without access gets an empty page. A row appears when the caller
holds ``contract:read-metadata`` there, or ``contract:read-published`` and the contract has a
Latest. Every row is the contract's head: the Latest once one exists (for every caller), else
the newest draft. Its content-derived fields are filled only where the caller holds
``contract:read`` or ``contract:read-published``, and content filters match only those
rows, so a published-only caller can never match a draft's values.

400.description: Bad request (for example an encoded slash or NUL in the path)

403.description: The caller may see the resource but not perform the operation

422.description: Invalid limit, cursor or filter value

get.description:
Contract metadata of the head row; content-derived fields are null without ``contract:read``.

The head row is the Latest once the contract has one, else the newest draft.
``contract:view`` admits every role that can see contracts; a caller who holds
``contract:read-published`` only gets the Latest (published content they may fetch anyway),
and the unknown-contract 404 for a contract without one.
